beats.say: Your phone just threw about thirty thousand invisible dots at your face, and you never saw a thing.
A tiny projector fires infrared dots. You can't see them, but a special camera can.
Infrared works in total darkness, so your phone can read your face even with the lights off.
The dot pattern bends over your nose and cheeks. How far each dot shifts tells the camera how deep that spot is.
From thousands of those shifts, it builds a depth map of your face. A 3D shape, not a flat picture.
That map is turned into a pattern of numbers and kept in a secure chip inside the phone. Not a photo.
Next time, it scans again and compares the new pattern with the stored one. Close enough, and it unlocks.
It even adapts a little over time, as your face changes, with glasses, a beard, or a new haircut.
A flat photo has no depth, so a simple picture of you fails.
Follow for how things work, in a minute.
